text: The Anti-Mechon Glaive (Japanese: , Gunshiki Chōtō: Kizan, Military Longsword: Machine Killer) is a weapon in . It is a sword wielded by Dunban. It is the first Anti-Mechon Weapon in the game aside from the Monado, and is Dunban's initial weapon when he rejoins the party after they exit the Ether Mine. It was made for him by Dickson. It is an improved version of the Homs Sabre, having, as with all the Anti-Mechon Weapons, the ability to damage Mechon. Despite its name, the Anti-Mechon Glaive is not really a Glaive due to not being a polearm weapon, but instead appears to be a katana. It cannot be traded for, bought or dropped in chests. It can, however, be sold.

Amethyst Gear (Japanese: , Ameshisuto Gia) is medium head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be bought at Sword Valley for 12,000 G, or be obtained as a quest reward after completing Mystery of Makna Ruins 1. It is made from nocturnal iron ore from Valak Mountain. It is part of the Amethyst set of armour along with the Amethyst Armour, Amethyst Gauntlets, Amethyst Leggings and Amethyst Boots.

Amethyst Gauntlets are medium arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Mystery of Makna Ruins 2, and can be bought at Sword Valley for 9,600 G. They are made from the nocturnal iron ore of Valak Mountain.
Amethyst Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be bought at Sword Valley for 19,200 G. They are made with nocturnal iron ore from Valak Mountain.

The Annihilator is a structure and weapon in . It harnesses the power of Black Fog to weaponize the Annihilation Event phenomenon. There are two known in existence, one for each nation's Castle.
Argos Boots are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the Argos Set and can be acquired from the First Sanctum during the second visit to Prison Island.

Argos Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the Argos Set. They can be found inside a Giants' Treasure Chest during the second visit to Prison Island by lowering the Bone Pillar and entering the revealed rooms at the sides of the Central Hall.
Argos Armour is medium torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is part of the Argos Set and can only be found in the Second Sanctum during the second visit to Prison Island.
Attack V Arms are Mechonis arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Glory and Gloria Slobos on Valak Mountain. They are not otherwise obtainable.

Arts Plus is a Blade Art in . It grants the Driver a buff that increases the damage dealt by the next Driver Art used by 50%. This effect has no duration and persists across Blade Switches, allowing it to be applied to any art across any of the engaged Blades' weapons. The AC Arts Boost Arts Card grants Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ access to this Blade Art, with cooldown that varies with equipment rank. The effect power of this art can be boosted using Board Game Pouch Item effects, increasing the next art's damage by up to 100% at maximum.

Azami (Japanese: ) is a Rare Blade in . She can grant tremendous power to her Drivers, Rex, Nia, Zeke or Mòrag, and their allies. Azami uses the dark element, wields an Ether Cannon, and acts as an Attacker in battle. She is a cybernetic woman with a dubious charm. Contrary to appearances, Azami has two normal hands, with her cannon having ten large finger-shaped decorations. Azami was designed by hakus, who also designed Dagas.

Back Attack Up is a Blade Art in . It grants the Driver a buff that increases damage dealt from the back by 50% and halves all aggro generated from back attacks for 15 seconds. This effect persists across Blade Switches. The AC Back Attack Up Arts Card grants Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ access to this Blade Art, with cooldown that varies with equipment rank. The effect power of this art can be boosted using Board Game Pouch Item effects, increasing damage dealt from the back by up to 100% at maximum. The duration of the buff can be extended up to 22.5s with the effects of the Helping Hand Aux Core or Skill RAM.
Bind: Refuel is a ground armor Skell Augment in and that increases the amount of fuel regenerated when Binding an enemy.

Blade Combos are battle mechanics in and . They are combined Specials with specified elements performed by Blades. By successfully chaining Specials together to continue the Blade Combo, the damage dealt to enemies increases, and one of the enemy's abilities can be sealed to cause certain effects on enemy or allies. To contribute to the combo, the Special used must be equal to or greater than the combo level. For example, if an enemy suffers "Heat" and the player wants to use Water to cause "Steam Bomb" (see the table below), the Water Special must be of level II or higher. Crush: Gain TP is a ground weapon special Augment in and that causes TP gain when destroying an enemy appendage.
Crush.GP is a Skell armor special augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts GP by 50 to 250 when destroying an enemy appendage with a Skell.
Custom.WP-STABLE is a Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts weapon stability, thereby reducing the Skell's damage spread. It is the Skell equivalent of the Stabilizer.
Custom.WP-ATK is a Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases the damage of the Skell weapon the augment is attached to. It is the Skell equivalent of Weapon Attack Power Up.
Custom.WP-DESTABLE is a Skell Weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It reduces weapon stability, thereby increasing the Skell's damage spread. It is the Skell equivalent of the Destabilizer.

Cressidus (Japanese: , Ootsuchi) is a Special Rare Blade in . He can grant tremendous power to his Driver Mikhail and his allies. Cressidus uses the earth element, wields a pair of Rockrending Gauntlets called the Royal Guard, and acts as a Tank in battle. __TOC__

Crossette (Japanese: , Hibana) is a Rare Blade in . She can grant tremendous power to her Drivers, Rex, Nia, Mòrag or Zeke, and their allies. Crossette uses the Fire element, wields a Bitball, and acts as a Healer in battle. She can be awakened from the Ebullient Core Crystal after getting the A Firecracker of a Gal Key Item upon installation of the Patch (Ver.1.5.1) and the New Rare Blade Pack 2 from the Expansion Pass. Crossette was designed by Atto (Japanese: ).

Corvin (Japanese: , Kamuya; English dub: ) is a Rare Blade in . He can grant tremendous power to his Drivers, Rex, Nia, Zeke or Mòrag, and their allies. Corvin uses the Light element, wields an Uchigatana, and acts as a Tank in battle. Any Driver bonded with Corvin can use an art that inflicts Smash. After installing the version 1.5.2 update and getting the A Boy of Two Swords Key Item, Corvin can be awakened from the Divine Core Crystal, which is given to the party by Sorinosori at the Argentum Trade Guild Chapter 2 onwards. He is the third and final Rare Blade introduced in the Expansion Pass. Corvin is designed by Shingo Adachi, character designer for the Sword Art Online series.

The Daedalus (Japanese: , Daidarosu) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn, and, unlike most other weapons, can only be obtained from the Giants' Treasure Chest in the First Sanctum of Prison Island.

Dagas (Japanese: , Kubira) is a Rare Blade in . He can grant tremendous power to his Drivers, Rex, Nia, Zeke or Mòrag, and their allies. Dagas uses the fire element, wields a Greataxe, and acts as an Attacker in battle. He is gorgeously dressed and has a noble aura. Dagas was designed by hakus, who also designed Azami.

Dahlia (Japanese: , Tsuki) is a Rare Blade in . She can grant tremendous power to her Drivers, Rex, Nia, Zeke or Mòrag, and their allies. Dahlia uses the ice element, wields a Bitball, and acts as a Healer in battle. Dahlia was designed by Risa Ebata (Satelight Inc.), a character designer and animator for Macross Frontier, who also designed Ursula.

Dickson (Japanese: , Dikuson, Dikson; English dub: ) is a veteran of the Battle of Sword Valley a year before the events of and a comrade of Dunban and Mumkhar. He is a resident of Colony 9 and looks over Shulk, Reyn and the other residents. He claims to have found Shulk on Valak Mountain with the Monado, and his parents (alongside their entire research group) dead. Dickson raised Shulk as his own.
Destabilizer is a ground weapon mod Augment in and that reduces weapon stability, thereby increasing the weapon's damage spread. The Skell equivalent is Custom.WP-DESTABLE.

Dolmes (Japanese: , Dorumesu) is a Special Blade in . He can grant tremendous power to his Driver Dughall. Dolmes uses the fire element, and wields a Spiked Hammer, which Dughall can use in battle. __TOC__

Eclipse Gear (Japanese: , Ekuripusu Gia) is heavy head armour in . It can be dropped by various Nebulae during the second visit to Prison Island.

Dromarch (Japanese: , Byakko) is a Blade in . He has the power to heal allies while attacking when bonded to his Driver, Nia. Dromarch uses the water element, wields a Twin Rings, and acts as a Healer in battle. He takes on the appearance of a white tiger. He refers to Nia as "My Lady" (, Ojōsama), as if he were a butler. When Nia is the lead character with Dromarch as her on-field Blade, she rides on his back as she does in cutscenes.

Electra (Japanese: , Raiko) is a Rare Blade in . She can grant tremendous power to her Drivers, Rex, Nia, Zeke or Mòrag, and their allies. Electra uses the electric element, wields a Shield Hammer, and acts as a Tank in battle. She has the appearance of a young girl, and has a positive temperament. Electra was designed by Asato Mizu, creator of the Denkigai no Honya-san manga series.

Ether Burst (Japanese: , Ēterubāsuto) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a staff wielded by Melia that can only be acquired from a chest in the First Sanctum on Prison Island.

She puts on this mask during her specials, and it seems to be the source of an alter-ego. KOS-MOS, short for Kosmos Obey Strategical Multiple Operation System, (Japanese: , KOS-MOS Re:) is a Rare Blade in . She can grant tremendous power to her Drivers, Rex, Nia, Zeke or Mòrag, and their allies. KOS-MOS uses the light element, wields an Ether Cannon, and acts as an Attacker in battle. KOS-MOS is a featured character based on KOS-MOS from the Xenosaga series. She is an armored android combat weapon with an artificial intelligence. Her design is based on the KOS-MOS's Version 1 model from Xenosaga Episode I: Der Wille zur Macht; both the original and redesign are by Kunihiko Tanaka, who also designed Finch, Elma, Fiora and Shulk in . KOS-MOS' cannons' design resembles the Zohar.

Titan Helms (Japanese: , Titān Herumu) are heavy head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. One can be found on the second visit to Prison Island by lowering the Bone Pillar and entering the revealed rooms by the foot of the main staircase in Central Hall.
